Method of Attack: Phishing attacks distributing password-protected ZIP archives containing ISO or IMG images with malicious files
Exploitation of a Windows zero-day vulnerability that prevents Mark of the Web security warnings from displaying
Use of JavaScript files signed with malformed embedded base64 encoded signature blocks to bypass security warnings
Malware loader injecting DLL into legitimate Windows processes to evade detection
Distribution of ransomware via JavaScript files executed by Windows Script Host
Impacted Systems: Windows processes such as wermgr.exe, AtBroker.exe
Attack Vector: Phishing emails with links to password-protected ZIP archives
Malicious JavaScript files executed via Windows Script Host (wscript.exe)
Malicious ISO and IMG disk images mounted as drives containing malware components
Indicators of Compromise: Password-protected ZIP archives containing nested ZIP and IMG files
JS files with malformed embedded base64 encoded signature blocks
Files named WW.js, data.txt, resemblance.tmp (DLL renamed to .tmp)
Emails containing links to malicious archives and passwords
